source_refs.note: PDF 265-270 (book p. 263-268): cot x, Figure 9.14, principal cotangent function, cot^-1, Figures 9.15(a)/(b), Examples 2-7, summary table of domains and ranges

blocks.text: Yeh is section ka aakhri inverse function hai: cotangent ka inverse. Is ke baad hum ek table mein saare chhe functions ke domains aur ranges ek jagah dekhenge, aur phir chhe solved examples se yeh saari baatein pakki karenge. Cotangent ek lehaz se tangent ka ulta hai, \(\cot x = \frac{1}{\tan x} = \frac{\cos x}{\sin x}\), magar is ka principal interval tangent wala nahin hoga. Kyun? Yahi is page ka pehla sabaq hai.
Function \(f(x) = \cot x\) ka domain \(\{x \mid x \in \mathbb{R} \wedge x \ne n\pi,\ n \in \mathbb{Z}\}\) aur range \((-\infty, \infty)\) hai. Is ka graph Figure 9.14 mein hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: \(\cot x = \frac{\cos x}{\sin x}\), is liye jahan \(\sin x = 0\) (yani \(x = n\pi\)) wahan cotangent define nahin; yahi vertical asymptotes hain. Range ke maamle mein cotangent, cosecant aur secant se mukhtalif hai: har branch par yeh \(+\infty\) se gir kar \(-\infty\) tak jata hai, raaste mein har real value leta hai. Is liye range poora \(\mathbb{R}\) hai, koi gap nahin.

blocks.alt: Graph of y = cot x for x from minus 2 pi to 2 pi. Dashed vertical asymptotes at x = minus 2 pi, minus pi, 0, pi and 2 pi. Between each pair of neighbouring asymptotes the curve falls from plus infinity to minus infinity, crossing the x-axis at the odd multiples of pi over 2. A dashed horizontal line y = 2 cuts every branch once.
blocks.caption: Figure 9.14: graph of \(y = \cot x\) from \(-2\pi\) to \(2\pi\) (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab ki Figure 9.14 ke \(x\)-axis par (jo \(\frac{\pi}{3}\) ke qadmon mein marked hai) \(-\pi\) wale point par sirf '\(\pi\)' likha hai; minus ka nishan reh gaya hai. Humari drawing mein axis \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) ke qadmon mein hai aur \(-\pi\) sahi likha hai.

Graph se saaf hai ke cotangent bijective nahin, kyun ke line \(y = 2\) graph ko bahut saare points par kaatti hai: har branch par ek dafa. Is liye domain ko interval \((0, \pi)\) tak restrict karte hain. Restricted function, yani \(f : (0, \pi) \to (-\infty, \infty)\), one-one aur onto ho jata hai, yani invertible hai, aur isay principal cotangent function kehte hain. Inverse cotangent function ki definition:

blocks.text_alt: y equals inverse cotangent of x if and only if x equals cotangent of y

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Tangent ki tarah \(\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\) kyun nahin liya? Kyun ke is interval ke bilkul beech mein \(x = 0\) hai, jahan \(\cot x\) define hi nahin (wahan \(\sin x = 0\)). Is interval mein cotangent ke do tootay hue tukde aate, aur har value do dafa milti. Interval \((0, \pi)\) par ek poori branch hai: \(\cot x\) lagataar \(+\infty\) se \(-\infty\) tak girta hai aur har real value bilkul ek dafa leta hai. Is liye yahi principal interval hai.

\(\cot^{-1} x\) ka domain \((-\infty, \infty)\) aur range \((0, \pi)\) hai. Yani kisi bhi real number ka \(\cot^{-1}\) nikal sakte hain (\(\csc^{-1}\) aur \(\sec^{-1}\) ki tarah koi pabandi nahin), aur jawab hamesha 0 aur \(\pi\) ke darmiyan aata hai.
Function \(\cot : (0, \pi) \to (-\infty, \infty)\) ka graph Figure 9.15(a) mein hai, aur \(\cot^{-1} : (-\infty, \infty) \to (0, \pi)\) ka graph Figure 9.15(b) mein.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab yahan 'Figure 15(a)' likhti hai. Sahi naam Figure 9.15(a) hai.

blocks.alt: Principal branch of y = cot x on the open interval 0 to pi. The curve falls from plus infinity near the y-axis, passes through (pi over 2, 0) and goes down to minus infinity near the dashed asymptote x = pi.
blocks.caption: Figure 9.15(a): graph of \(y = \cot x\) from 0 to \(\pi\) (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.alt: Graph of y = inverse cotangent of x for all real x. The curve decreases from near the dashed line y = pi on the far left, passes through (0, pi over 2), and approaches the x-axis on the far right without touching it.
blocks.caption: Figure 9.15(b): graph of \(y = \cot^{-1} x\) (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Figure 9.15(a) ko line \(y = x\) mein palat dein to Figure 9.15(b) milti hai: point \(\left(\frac{\pi}{2}, 0\right)\) ban jata hai \(\left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\). Vertical asymptotes \(x = 0\) aur \(x = \pi\) ab horizontal asymptotes \(y = 0\) aur \(y = \pi\) ban gaye. Matlab \(\cot^{-1} x\) hamesha 0 aur \(\pi\) ke beech rehta hai, kabhi negative nahin. Misal: \(\cot^{-1}(-1) = \frac{3\pi}{4}\), \(-\frac{\pi}{4}\) nahin. Bahut se students yahan tangent wali aadat se negative jawab likh dete hain.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Kya \(\cot^{-1} x\) kabhi \(\pi\) ke barabar ho sakta hai? Iske liye \(x = \cot\pi\) chahiye, jo define nahin. Aur 0? \(\cot 0\) bhi define nahin. Is liye range ke dono kinare (end points) khule (open) hain: \((0, \pi)\).

Ab tak hum ne chhe inverse functions ki definitions, domains aur ranges dekhi hain. Ab examples ki baari hai. Har example mein ek hi sunehri usool yaad rakhiye: inverse function ka jawab hamesha us ki principal range mein hona chahiye. Zyada tar ghaltiyan isi usool ko bhoolne se hoti hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Is qisam ke sawalon (jaise \(\sec[\tan^{-1} a]\)) ko hal karne ka ek pakka nuskha hai. Pehla qadam: andar wale inverse function ko \(y\) ka naam dein. Doosra: definition se usay aam equation banayein, jaise \(\tan y = a\). Teesra: principal range ke andar woh angle dhoondein. Chautha: us angle par bahar wala function lagayein. Jab tak aap is tarteeb par chalenge, ghalti ka imkaan bahut kam hai. Sab se zyada ghalti teesre qadam mein hoti hai, jab student range ka khayal kiye baghair koi bhi angle utha leta hai.

blocks.title: Example 2
steps:
Diya gaya: teen expressions, har ek mein kisi inverse trigonometric value ka trigonometric function liya gaya hai.
Maloom karna: har expression ki value.
Tareeqa: andar se bahar ki taraf kaam karenge. Pehle andar wala angle nikalenge (inverse function ki principal value, jo us ki principal range ke andar ho), phir us angle par bahar wala function lagayenge. Bilkul aise jaise bracket wale sawal mein pehle bracket hal karte hain.

(i) Andar wale angle ko naam dein
\[\tan^{-1}(-\sqrt{3}) = y\]
\[\tan y = -\sqrt{3}\]
\[y \in \left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\]
Kyun: definition kehti hai \(y = \tan^{-1} x \iff x = \tan y\). Aur \(\tan^{-1}\) ki principal value hamesha \(\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\) mein hoti hai, is liye jawab isi interval mein dhoondna hai.

(i) \(y\) maloom karein
\[\tan y = -\sqrt{3} = \tan\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)\]
\[y = -\dfrac{\pi}{3}\]
Yani \(\tan^{-1}(-\sqrt{3}) = -\frac{\pi}{3}\).
Kyun: \(\tan\frac{\pi}{3} = \sqrt{3}\) hum jaante hain, aur tangent odd function hai (\(\tan(-\theta) = -\tan\theta\)). Dhyan dein: \(\frac{2\pi}{3}\) ka tangent bhi \(-\sqrt{3}\) hai, magar woh principal range se bahar hai, is liye nahin chalega.

(i) Ab secant lagayein
\[\sec\left[\tan^{-1}(-\sqrt{3})\right]\]
\[= \sec\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = \dfrac{1}{\cos\frac{\pi}{3}}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{1/2} = 2\]
Kyun: \(\sec\theta = \frac{1}{\cos\theta}\), aur cosine even function hai, yani \(\cos\left(-\frac{\pi}{3}\right) = \cos\frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{1}{2}\). Minus sign yahan khud ba khud ghayab ho gaya.

(ii) Andar wale angle ko naam dein
\[\cos^{-1}\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = y\]
Pehle woh angle \(y\) dhoondte hain jis ka cosine \(-\frac{1}{2}\) hai:
\[\cos y = -\dfrac{1}{2},\quad y \in [0, \pi]\]
Kyun: \(\cos^{-1}\) ki principal range \([0, \pi]\) hai. (Kitab is jagah ek ghalat jumla chhaapti hai; neeche 'Kitab ki ghalti' dekhiye.)

(ii) \(y\) maloom karein
\[\cos y = -\dfrac{1}{2} = \cos\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\]
\[y = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}\]
Kyun: \(\cos\frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{1}{2}\), aur rule \(\cos(\pi - \theta) = -\cos\theta\) se \(\cos\frac{2\pi}{3} = -\frac{1}{2}\). Yeh angle \([0, \pi]\) mein hai. Dhyan dein: \(-\frac{\pi}{3}\) ka cosine to \(+\frac{1}{2}\) hai, woh yahan bilkul ghalat hoga.

(ii) Ab cotangent lagayein
\[\cot\dfrac{2\pi}{3} = \dfrac{\cos\frac{2\pi}{3}}{\sin\frac{2\pi}{3}}\]
\[= \dfrac{-1/2}{\sqrt{3}/2} = -\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\]
Kyun: \(\cot\theta = \frac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}\). Second quadrant mein sine positive hota hai: \(\sin\frac{2\pi}{3} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\). Dono ke 2 cancel ho gaye.

(iii) Andar wala angle
\[\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = y\]
\[\sin y = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2},\ y \in \left[-\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]\]
\[\sin y = \sin\dfrac{\pi}{3} \Rightarrow y = \dfrac{\pi}{3}\]
Kyun: \(\sin\frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\), aur \(\frac{\pi}{3}\) \(\sin^{-1}\) ki principal range mein hai.

(iii) Ab cosecant lagayein
\[\csc\left[\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)\right]\]
\[= \csc\dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\]
Kyun: \(\csc\theta = \frac{1}{\sin\theta}\), to \(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\) ka ulta \(\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\). Ek chhota shortcut bhi dekh lijiye: \(\csc(\sin^{-1} t) = \frac{1}{t}\) jab \(t \ne 0\), kyun ke andar wale angle ka sine \(t\) hi to hai.

Tasdeeq:
(i) \(\cos\left(-\frac{\pi}{3}\right) = \frac{1}{2}\), us ka ulta 2.
(ii) Calculator se: \(\cos^{-1}(-0.5) \approx 2.0944\) aur \(\cot 2.0944 \approx -0.5774 = -\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\).
(iii) \(\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}} \approx 1.1547\), jo \(\frac{1}{0.8660}\) ke barabar hai. Teeno jawab sahi.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Example 2(ii) mein kitab likhti hai: 'First, we find the angle 1, whose cosine is \(-\sqrt{3}\).' Yeh do jagah ghalat hai. Angle ka naam \(y\) hai (1 nahin), aur us ka cosine \(-\frac{1}{2}\) hai. \(-\sqrt{3}\) to kisi angle ka cosine ho hi nahin sakta, kyun ke cosine hamesha \(-1\) aur \(1\) ke darmiyan hota hai. Sahi jumla: 'Pehle woh angle \(y\) dhoondte hain jis ka cosine \(-\frac{1}{2}\) hai.' Baqi hal aur jawab \(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\) sahi hain.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Ab khud try kijiye: \(\sec\left[\cos^{-1}\frac{1}{3}\right]\) kitna hoga? Andar wale angle ka cosine \(\frac{1}{3}\) hai, to us ka secant (ulta) 3 hoga. Aur \(\tan\left[\cot^{-1}(-1)\right]\)? Andar wala angle \(\frac{3\pi}{4}\) hai (range \((0, \pi)\) yaad rakhiye), aur \(\tan\frac{3\pi}{4} = -1\). Dekha, jawab nikalne se pehle range ka sahi istemal kitna zaroori hai.

Neeche di gayi table principal trigonometric functions aur inverse trigonometric functions ke domains aur ranges ka khulasa (summary) hai. Ise ratne ke bajaye samajhiye: upar ke chhe rows principal functions hain, neeche ke chhe un ke inverses.

blocks.caption: Domains and ranges of the principal trigonometric functions (first six rows) and the inverse trigonometric functions (last six rows); the book prints the two halves side by side

blocks.title: Teaching note

blocks.text: Ab ek bilkul naya sawal: kisi function ka domain kaise nikalein jis ke andar inverse trigonometric function ho? Is mein koi naya formula nahin, sirf ek baat: har inverse function har number qubool nahin karta. Upar wali table ka 'Domain' column yahan kaam aayega. Hum andar wali expression ko us domain mein rakhte hain aur inequality hal karte hain.

blocks.title: Example 3
blocks.problem: Find the domain of the following functions (i) \(f(x) = \cos^{-1}(3x - 1)\) (ii) \(g(x) = \sin^{-1}\left(\frac{x^{2} - 5}{4}\right)\) (iii) \(h(x) = \sec^{-1}(\ln x)\)
steps:
Diya gaya: teen functions jo inverse trigonometric functions se bane hain.
Maloom karna: har function ka domain, yani woh saari \(x\) values jin par function define ho.
Tareeqa: har inverse function sirf apne domain se input leta hai. \(\cos^{-1}\) aur \(\sin^{-1}\) ko input \([-1, 1]\) mein chahiye; \(\sec^{-1}\) ko \((-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\) mein. Is liye andar wali expression ko is shart mein rakh kar inequality hal karenge. Yeh aise hai jaise kisi machine mein sirf khaas size ka sikka dala ja sakta hai: hum dekh rahe hain ke kaun se \(x\) sahi size ka sikka banate hain.

(i) Shart likhein
\(\cos^{-1} x\) sirf un \(x\) ke liye define hai jin ke liye \(-1 \le x \le 1\). Yahan input \(3x - 1\) hai, is liye:
\[-1 \le 3x - 1 \le 1\]
Kyun: jo cheez \(\cos^{-1}\) ke andar hai, usi par shart lagti hai, \(x\) par seedha nahin.

(i) Hal karein
\[0 \le 3x \le 2\]
\[0 \le x \le \dfrac{2}{3}\]
\[x \in \left[0, \dfrac{2}{3}\right]\]
Kyun: teeno hisson mein 1 jama kiya, phir teeno ko 3 se divide kiya. 3 positive hai, is liye inequality ke nishan nahin palte. Domain \(\left[0, \frac{2}{3}\right]\) hai.

(ii) Shart likhein
\[-1 \le \dfrac{x^{2} - 5}{4} \le 1\]
\[-4 \le x^{2} - 5 \le 4\]
\[1 \le x^{2} \le 9\]
Kyun: \(\sin^{-1}\) ka input \([-1, 1]\) mein hona chahiye. Teeno hisson ko 4 se multiply kiya, phir 5 jama kiya.

(ii) Do sharton mein todein
\[x^{2} \ge 1 \Rightarrow x \le -1 \text{ or } x \ge 1\]
yani \(x \in (-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\), aur
\[x^{2} \le 9 \Rightarrow (x - 3)(x + 3) \le 0\]
yani \(x \in [-3, 3]\).
Kyun: \(x^{2} \ge 1\) ka matlab \(|x| \ge 1\), yani \(x\) zero se kam az kam 1 door ho. Do factors ka product \(\le 0\) tab hota hai jab un ke sign ulte hon, aur yeh roots \(-3\) aur \(3\) ke darmiyan hota hai. Dhyan dein: \(x^{2} \ge 1\) se sirf \(x \ge 1\) likh dena aam ghalti hai; negative wala hissa mat bhooliye.

(ii) Mushtarka hissa (intersection) lein
\[x \in [-3, -1] \cup [1, 3]\]
Kyun: dono sharten ek saath poori honi chahiyein, is liye sirf woh \(x\) rakhenge jo dono sets mein hain. Number line par socheiye: \([-3, 3]\) mein se beech wala \((-1, 1)\) nikal diya. Yeh \(g(x)\) ka domain hai.

(iii) Sharten likhein
\(\sec^{-1}\) ka domain \((-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\) hai, is liye
\[\ln x \ge 1 \ \text{ or } \ \ln x \le -1\]
Is ke saath \(\ln x\) khud bhi sirf \(x > 0\) par maujood hai.
Kyun: \(\sec^{-1}\) ka input \(\ln x\) hai. Aur logarithm sirf positive number ka hota hai. Yeh doosri shart hi woh hai jo kitab bhool gayi.

(iii) Hal karein
\[\ln x \ge 1 \Rightarrow x \ge e\]
\[\ln x \le -1 \Rightarrow 0 < x \le e^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{e}\]
Kyun: \(e^{x}\) increasing function hai, is liye dono taraf \(e\) ki power lene se inequality ka nishan wahi rehta hai: \(x = e^{\ln x} \ge e^{1}\), ya \(x \le e^{-1}\). Saath hi \(x > 0\) ki shart lagani zaroori hai.

(iii) Domain
\[x \in \left(0, \dfrac{1}{e}\right] \cup [e, \infty)\]
Kyun: dono tukde jor diye, sirf positive \(x\) rakh kar. Misal: \(x = -1\) nahin chal sakta kyun ke \(\ln(-1)\) maujood hi nahin.

Tasdeeq:
(i) \(x = 0\): \(\cos^{-1}(-1) = \pi\) maujood hai; \(x = 1\): \(\cos^{-1}(2)\) maujood nahin.
(ii) \(x = \pm 3\): \(\frac{9 - 5}{4} = 1\), theek; \(x = 0\): \(-\frac{5}{4} < -1\), nahin chalega.
(iii) \(x = e\): \(\sec^{-1}(1) = 0\) maujood; \(x = 1\): \(\sec^{-1}(0)\) maujood nahin.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text:
Example 3 mein teen ghaltiyan hain.
(i) Kitab domain \(\left[0, \frac{2}{3}\right]\) likhne ke baad 'such that \(-1 \le x \le 1\)' bhi likh deti hai. Yeh faltu tukda hai; domain sirf \(\left[0, \frac{2}{3}\right]\) hai.
(ii) Kitab natije mein function ko \(f(x)\) kehti hai, jab ke sawal mein yeh \(g(x) = \sin^{-1}\left(\frac{x^{2} - 5}{4}\right)\) hai. Domain \([-3, -1] \cup [1, 3]\) sahi hai.
(iii) Kitab \(h(x) = \sec^{-1}(\ln x)\) ka domain \(\left(-\infty, \frac{1}{e}\right] \cup [e, \infty)\) likhti hai. Magar \(\ln x\) sirf \(x > 0\) par define hai, is liye sahi domain \(\left(0, \frac{1}{e}\right] \cup [e, \infty)\) hai.

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text: Domain ke sawal mein jawab hamesha interval ki shakal mein likhiye aur brackets ka khayal rakhiye: jo end point shamil hai us par square bracket \([\ ]\), jo shamil nahin us par round bracket \((\ )\). Aur aakhir mein ek-do values rakh kar check zaroor kijiye, khaas taur par end points aur koi aisa number jo bahar hona chahiye. Agar andar \(\ln x\), \(\sqrt{x}\) ya kisi fraction ka denominator ho, to us ki apni shart bhi likhiye.

Agli do examples mein hum kuch aham rishte (identities) saabit karenge jo aage Exercise 9.1 aur 9.2 mein baar baar kaam aayenge. In ka faida yeh hai ke \(\csc^{-1}\), \(\sec^{-1}\) aur \(\cot^{-1}\) ke sawal hum jaane pehchane \(\sin^{-1}\), \(\cos^{-1}\) aur \(\tan^{-1}\) mein badal sakte hain, jin ki values humein zabani yaad hain.

blocks.title: Example 4
blocks.problem: Prove that: (i) \(\csc^{-1} x = \sin^{-1}\frac{1}{x},\ x \in (-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\) (ii) \(\sec^{-1} x = \cos^{-1}\frac{1}{x},\ x \in (-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\) (iii) \(\cot^{-1} x = \tan^{-1}\frac{1}{x},\ x \in (0, \infty)\)
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\csc^{-1}\), \(\sec^{-1}\) aur \(\cot^{-1}\) ki definitions.
Maloom karna (saabit karna): har ek ko reciprocal function ke inverse mein \(\frac{1}{x}\) par likha ja sakta hai.
Tareeqa: left side ko \(y\) maan lein, definition se usay aam trigonometric equation bana dein, reciprocal identity lagayein, aur phir usay doosre inverse function ki shakal mein wapas parhein. Aakhir mein check karein ke \(y\) naye inverse function ki principal range mein hai.

Proof (i): shuruaat
Maan lein \(\csc^{-1} x = y\), to
\[x = \csc y\]
Kyun: definition \(y = \csc^{-1} x \iff x = \csc y\), jahan \(y \in \left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, 0\right) \cup \left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\).

Proof (i): reciprocal lein
\[\sin y = \dfrac{1}{x}\]
\[y = \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right)\]
Is liye
\[\csc^{-1} x = \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right)\]
Kyun: \(\csc y = \frac{1}{\sin y}\), to \(\sin y = \frac{1}{x}\) (yahan \(x \ne 0\)). \(|x| \ge 1\) hai, to \(\left|\frac{1}{x}\right| \le 1\), yani \(\sin^{-1}\frac{1}{x}\) maujood hai. Aur \(y\) \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) mein hai, jo \(\sin^{-1}\) ki principal range hai, is liye \(y\) bilkul \(\sin^{-1}\frac{1}{x}\) hi hai. Yeh check zaroori hai, warna sirf 'sine barabar hai' kehne se angle barabar nahin ho jate.

Proof (ii)
Maan lein \(\sec^{-1} x = y\), to \(x = \sec y\).
\[\cos y = \dfrac{1}{x}\]
\[y = \cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right)\]
Is liye \(\sec^{-1} x = \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)\).
Kyun: \(\sec y = \frac{1}{\cos y}\). Aur \(y \in \left[0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right) \cup \left(\frac{\pi}{2}, \pi\right]\) poora \([0, \pi]\) ke andar hai, jo \(\cos^{-1}\) ki principal range hai.

Proof (iii)
Maan lein \(\cot^{-1} x = y\), to \(x = \cot y\).
\[\tan y = \dfrac{1}{x}\]
\[y = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right)\]
Is liye \(\cot^{-1} x = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)\).
Kyun: \(\tan y = \frac{1}{\cot y}\). \(x > 0\) ho to \(y = \cot^{-1} x\) \(\left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\) mein hota hai, jo \(\tan^{-1}\) ki range \(\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\) ke andar hai. Isi liye kitab ne yahan \(x \in (0, \infty)\) ki shart lagayi hai.

Tasdeeq:
(i) \(x = 2\): \(\csc^{-1} 2 = \frac{\pi}{6}\) aur \(\sin^{-1}\frac{1}{2} = \frac{\pi}{6}\).
(ii) \(x = -2\): \(\sec^{-1}(-2) = \frac{2\pi}{3}\) aur \(\cos^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) = \frac{2\pi}{3}\).
(iii) \(x = \sqrt{3}\): \(\cot^{-1}\sqrt{3} = \frac{\pi}{6}\) aur \(\tan^{-1}\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{\pi}{6}\). Teeno barabar.
blocks.answer: Saabit ho gaya: \(\csc^{-1} x = \sin^{-1}\frac{1}{x}\), \(\sec^{-1} x = \cos^{-1}\frac{1}{x}\) (jab \(|x| \ge 1\)), aur \(\cot^{-1} x = \tan^{-1}\frac{1}{x}\) (jab \(x > 0\)).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: (iii) mein \(x > 0\) ki shart kyun zaroori hai? \(x < 0\) ho to \(\cot^{-1} x\) \(\left(\frac{\pi}{2}, \pi\right)\) mein hota hai, jo \(\tan^{-1}\) ki range se bahar hai. Misal: \(\cot^{-1}(-1) = \frac{3\pi}{4}\), magar \(\tan^{-1}(-1) = -\frac{\pi}{4}\). Dono barabar nahin! Negative \(x\) ke liye sahi rishta \(\cot^{-1} x = \pi + \tan^{-1}\frac{1}{x}\) hai. (i) aur (ii) mein aisi koi shart nahin chahiye, kyun ke wahan ranges pehle hi fit hain.

Example 5 mein teen khoobsurat natije hain: har inverse function aur us ke 'co-function' (sine ke saath cosine, cosecant ke saath secant, tangent ke saath cotangent) ka jama hamesha \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) hota hai. Kitab sirf pehla hissa hal karti hai aur baqi do 'similarly' keh kar chhor deti hai. Hum ne neeche teeno ka poora hal diya hai, taa ke aap dekh sakein ke 'similarly' ke peeche asal mein kya kaam hota hai.

blocks.title: Example 5
blocks.problem: Prove that (i) \(\sin^{-1} x + \cos^{-1} x = \frac{\pi}{2},\ x \in [-1, 1]\) (ii) \(\csc^{-1} x + \sec^{-1} x = \frac{\pi}{2},\ x \in (-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\) (iii) \(\tan^{-1} x + \cot^{-1} x = \frac{\pi}{2},\ x \in (-\infty, \infty)\)
steps:
Diya gaya: \(x\) di gayi domains mein.
Maloom karna (saabit karna): har 'co-function' jori ka jama \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) hai.
Tareeqa: \(\sin^{-1} x = y\) maan kar \(x = \sin y\) ko cosine ki shakal mein likhenge, identity \(\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - \alpha\right) = \sin\alpha\) se, aur phir usay \(\cos^{-1}\) ke taur par wapas parhenge. Sochiye: right triangle mein do acute angles ka jama \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) hota hai, aur ek ka sine doosre ka cosine hota hai. Yahi khayal yahan kaam kar raha hai.

(i) Shuruaat
Maan lein \(\sin^{-1} x = y\)
\[x = \sin y = \cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - y\right)\]
Kyun: \(\sin^{-1}\) ki definition (\(y \in \left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\)), aur co-function identity \(\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - \alpha\right) = \sin\alpha\).

(i) \(\cos^{-1}\) ki shakal mein parhein
\[x = \cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - y\right)\]
\[\cos^{-1} x = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - y\]
Kyun: \(-\frac{\pi}{2} \le y \le \frac{\pi}{2}\) se \(0 \le \frac{\pi}{2} - y \le \pi\) milta hai, jo \(\cos^{-1}\) ki principal range hai. Kitab yeh baat nahin likhti, magar isi se yeh qadam jaaiz (valid) hai.

(i) Tarteeb dein
\[\cos^{-1} x + y = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\]
\[\cos^{-1} x + \sin^{-1} x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\]
Kyun: dono taraf \(y\) jama kiya aur \(y = \sin^{-1} x\) wapas rakh diya. (i) saabit.

(ii) Hamara hal (kitab sirf itna kehti hai: 'Similarly, we can prove (ii) and (iii)')
Example 4 se, \(|x| \ge 1\) ke liye:
\[\csc^{-1} x + \sec^{-1} x\]
\[= \sin^{-1}\dfrac{1}{x} + \cos^{-1}\dfrac{1}{x}\]
\[= \dfrac{\pi}{2}\]
Kyun: \(t = \frac{1}{x}\) \([-1, 1]\) mein hai, is liye (i) wala natija \(t\) par lagta hai. Pichhli example ka natija agli mein kaam aa gaya.

(iii) Hamara hal
Maan lein \(\tan^{-1} x = y\), \(y \in \left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\).
\[x = \tan y = \cot\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - y\right)\]
\[\cot^{-1} x = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - y\]
\[\tan^{-1} x + \cot^{-1} x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\]
Kyun: identity \(\cot\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - \alpha\right) = \tan\alpha\); aur \(0 < \frac{\pi}{2} - y < \pi\), jo \(\cot^{-1}\) ki principal range hai.

Tasdeeq:
(i) \(x = \frac{1}{2}\): \(\frac{\pi}{6} + \frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{\pi}{2}\).
(ii) \(x = 2\): \(\frac{\pi}{6} + \frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{\pi}{2}\).
(iii) \(x = -1\): \(-\frac{\pi}{4} + \frac{3\pi}{4} = \frac{\pi}{2}\). Negative \(x\) par bhi natija sahi hai.
blocks.answer: Saabit ho gaya: \(\sin^{-1} x + \cos^{-1} x = \frac{\pi}{2}\), \(\csc^{-1} x + \sec^{-1} x = \frac{\pi}{2}\), \(\tan^{-1} x + \cot^{-1} x = \frac{\pi}{2}\) (di gayi domains par).

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text: Example 5 ka natija bahut kaam ka hai. Misal: agar \(\sin^{-1} x = \frac{\pi}{5}\) ho, to \(\cos^{-1} x\) nikalne ke liye \(x\) dhoondne ki zaroorat nahin: \(\cos^{-1} x = \frac{\pi}{2} - \frac{\pi}{5} = \frac{3\pi}{10}\). Isi tarah \(\tan^{-1} 3 + \cot^{-1} 3 = \frac{\pi}{2}\), seedha.

Example 6 mein do mukhtalif inverse functions ko barabar saabit karna hai. Aise sawal ka aam tareeqa yeh hai: ek taraf ke angle ko naam do, us ke saare trigonometric ratios nikalo, aur dekho ke doosri taraf wala ratio bhi wahi deta hai ya nahin. Aakhir mein range ka check lazmi hai, warna saboot adhoora rehta hai.

blocks.title: Example 6
steps:
Diya gaya: angle \(\cos^{-1}\frac{7}{25}\).
Maloom karna (saabit karna): yeh \(\csc^{-1}\frac{25}{24}\) ke barabar hai.
Tareeqa: angle ko \(\alpha\) ka naam denge, \(\cos\alpha\) se identity \(\sin^{2}\alpha + \cos^{2}\alpha = 1\) ke zariye \(\sin\alpha\) nikalenge, phir us ka ulta le kar \(\csc\alpha\) banayenge.

Angle ko naam dein
Maan lein \(\cos^{-1}\frac{7}{25} = \alpha\)
\[\cos\alpha = \dfrac{7}{25},\quad \alpha \in \left[0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]\]
Kyun: \(\cos^{-1}\) ki range \([0, \pi]\) hai, aur \(\frac{7}{25}\) positive hai, is liye angle pehle quadrant mein hai.

\(\sin\alpha\) nikalein
\[\sin\alpha = \pm\sqrt{1 - \cos^{2}\alpha}\]
\[= \pm\sqrt{1 - \left(\dfrac{7}{25}\right)^{2}}\]
\[= \pm\sqrt{\dfrac{625 - 49}{625}}\]
\[= \pm\sqrt{\dfrac{576}{625}} = \pm\dfrac{24}{25}\]
Kyun: \(\sin^{2}\alpha + \cos^{2}\alpha = 1\) se. Hisaab: \(25^{2} = 625\), \(7^{2} = 49\), aur \(\sqrt{576} = 24\).

Sign chunein
\[\sin\alpha = \dfrac{24}{25}\]
Kyun: \(\alpha\) pehle quadrant mein hai, jahan sine negative nahin hota. Is liye minus wala jawab chhor diya.

Ulta (reciprocal) lein
\[\csc\alpha = \dfrac{25}{24}\]
\[\alpha = \csc^{-1}\dfrac{25}{24}\]
Kyun: \(\csc\alpha = \frac{1}{\sin\alpha}\). Aur \(\alpha\) \(\left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) mein hai, jo \(\csc^{-1}\) ki principal range ke andar hai, is liye \(\alpha\) bilkul \(\csc^{-1}\frac{25}{24}\) hai. (Kitab yeh check chhor deti hai.)

Natija
\[\cos^{-1}\dfrac{7}{25} = \csc^{-1}\dfrac{25}{24}\]
Kyun: dono ek hi angle \(\alpha\) ke barabar hain.

Tasdeeq:
7, 24, 25 ek Pythagorean triple hai: \(7^{2} + 24^{2} = 49 + 576 = 625 = 25^{2}\). Ek right triangle sochiye jis mein adjacent side 7, opposite side 24 aur hypotenuse 25 ho. Us mein \(\cos\alpha = \frac{7}{25}\) aur \(\csc\alpha = \frac{25}{24}\). Calculator se dono angles taqreeban 1.2870 rad aate hain.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text: Isi tareeqe se dikhaiye ke \(\sin^{-1}\frac{3}{5} = \cot^{-1}\frac{4}{3}\). Maan lein \(\sin^{-1}\frac{3}{5} = \alpha\), to \(\sin\alpha = \frac{3}{5}\) aur \(\alpha\) pehle quadrant mein hai. Phir \(\cos\alpha = \frac{4}{5}\) (kyun ke \(1 - \frac{9}{25} = \frac{16}{25}\)), aur \(\cot\alpha = \frac{\cos\alpha}{\sin\alpha} = \frac{4}{3}\). \(\alpha\) \((0, \pi)\) mein hai, jo \(\cot^{-1}\) ki range hai, is liye \(\alpha = \cot^{-1}\frac{4}{3}\). Yahan 3, 4, 5 wala mashhoor triangle kaam aaya.

Aakhri example mein calculator ki ijazat nahin. Yahan asal kamaal yeh hai ke humein angle \(\alpha\) ki value (degrees ya radians mein) maloom karne ki zaroorat hi nahin. Humein sirf us ka cosine chahiye, jo tangent se ek chhote se triangle ke zariye mil jata hai. Phir half-angle identity baqi kaam kar deti hai.

blocks.title: Example 7
blocks.problem: Without using calculator find the value of \(\sin\left[\frac{1}{2}\tan^{-1}\frac{4}{3}\right]\).
steps:
Diya gaya: angle \(\tan^{-1}\frac{4}{3}\).
Maloom karna: is angle ke aadhe ka sine, calculator ke baghair.
Tareeqa: angle ko \(\alpha\) kahenge. \(\tan\alpha = \frac{4}{3}\) se point \((3, 4)\) bana kar \(\sin\alpha\) aur \(\cos\alpha\) nikalenge, phir half-angle identity \(\sin\frac{\alpha}{2} = \sqrt{\frac{1 - \cos\alpha}{2}}\) lagayenge. Yeh identity is liye chuni kyun ke is mein sirf \(\cos\alpha\) chahiye, jo hum aasani se nikal sakte hain.

Angle ko naam dein
Maan lein \(\tan^{-1}\frac{4}{3} = \alpha\)
\[\tan\alpha = \dfrac{4}{3}\]
Kyun: \(\tan^{-1}\) ki definition. \(\frac{4}{3}\) positive hai, is liye \(\alpha \in \left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\).

\(r\) nikalein
Yahan \(x = 3\), \(y = 4\)
\[r = \sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}}\]
\[= \sqrt{3^{2} + 4^{2}} = \sqrt{25} = 5\]
Kyun: \(\tan\alpha = \frac{y}{x}\), is liye hum \(\alpha\) ke terminal arm par point \((3, 4)\) le sakte hain. \(r\) us point ka origin se faasla hai (Pythagoras).

\(\sin\alpha\) aur \(\cos\alpha\)
\[\sin\alpha = \dfrac{y}{r} = \dfrac{4}{5}\]
\[\cos\alpha = \dfrac{x}{r} = \dfrac{3}{5}\]
Kyun: \(\sin\alpha = \frac{y}{r}\), \(\cos\alpha = \frac{x}{r}\). Jaanch: \(\frac{\sin\alpha}{\cos\alpha} = \frac{4/5}{3/5} = \frac{4}{3}\), jo \(\tan\alpha\) hi hai. Dhyan dein: kitab yahan dono values ulat deti hai (neeche 'Kitab ki ghalti' dekhiye).

Half-angle identity
\[\sin\dfrac{\alpha}{2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1 - \cos\alpha}{2}}\]
Kyun: yeh \(\cos\alpha = 1 - 2\sin^{2}\frac{\alpha}{2}\) se aati hai. Positive root is liye ke \(\frac{\alpha}{2} \in \left(0, \frac{\pi}{4}\right)\), jahan sine positive hai.

\(\cos\alpha = \frac{3}{5}\) rakhein
\[\sin\dfrac{\alpha}{2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1 - \frac{3}{5}}{2}}\]
\[= \sqrt{\dfrac{2/5}{2}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{5}}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\]
Kyun: \(1 - \frac{3}{5} = \frac{2}{5}\), aur \(\frac{2}{5}\) ko 2 se divide karein to \(\frac{1}{5}\). Kitab bhi is line mein sahi value \(\cos\alpha = \frac{3}{5}\) hi use karti hai, is liye us ka jawab sahi hai.

Tasdeeq:
\(\sin^{2}\frac{\alpha}{2} = \frac{1}{5}\) se \(\cos\frac{\alpha}{2} = \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\). Phir \(\sin\alpha = 2\sin\frac{\alpha}{2}\cos\frac{\alpha}{2} = 2 \cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \cdot \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} = \frac{4}{5}\), bilkul wahi jo upar nikla. Jawab pakka.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Example 7 mein \(x = 3\), \(y = 4\), \(r = 5\) lene ke baad kitab likhti hai: \(\sin\alpha = \frac{3}{5}\) aur \(\cos\alpha = \frac{4}{5}\). Yeh dono ulte hain. Sahi: \(\sin\alpha = \frac{y}{r} = \frac{4}{5}\) aur \(\cos\alpha = \frac{x}{r} = \frac{3}{5}\). Kitab ki agli line mein \(\cos\alpha = \frac{3}{5}\) hi istemal hua hai, is liye aakhri jawab \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\) sahi hai.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Isi example se \(\cos\left[\frac{1}{2}\tan^{-1}\frac{4}{3}\right]\) bhi nikal sakte hain: \(\cos\frac{\alpha}{2} = \sqrt{\frac{1 + \cos\alpha}{2}} = \sqrt{\frac{1 + 3/5}{2}} = \sqrt{\frac{4}{5}} = \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\). Check: \(\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\right)^{2} + \left(\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\right)^{2} = \frac{1}{5} + \frac{4}{5} = 1\). Bilkul theek.

Is tarah 9.1 ka poora hissa mukammal hua. Ab aap ke paas chhe inverse trigonometric functions, un ki ranges, graphs aur kuch aham rishte hain. Exercise 9.1 hal karte waqt har sawal mein sab se pehle khud se poochiye: is inverse function ki principal range kya hai? Yeh ek sawal aap ko aadhi ghaltiyon se bacha lega.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \(\cot x\): domain \(\mathbb{R} - \{n\pi\}\), range \(\mathbb{R}\). Principal cotangent function: \(\cot : (0, \pi) \to (-\infty, \infty)\).
2. \(y = \cot^{-1} x \iff x = \cot y\); domain \((-\infty, \infty)\), range \((0, \pi)\).
3. \(\sec[\tan^{-1} a]\) jaisi expression mein pehle andar wali principal value, phir bahar wala function.
4. Domain ke sawal mein andar wali expression ko inverse function ke domain mein rakh kar hal karein; \(\ln x\) ke liye \(x > 0\) jaisi izafi shart mat bhooliye.
5. \(\csc^{-1} x = \sin^{-1}\frac{1}{x}\), \(\sec^{-1} x = \cos^{-1}\frac{1}{x}\) (\(|x| \ge 1\)); \(\cot^{-1} x = \tan^{-1}\frac{1}{x}\) (\(x > 0\)).
6. \(\sin^{-1} x + \cos^{-1} x = \csc^{-1} x + \sec^{-1} x = \tan^{-1} x + \cot^{-1} x = \frac{\pi}{2}\).

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Negative number ka \(\cot^{-1}\) negative angle likhna: \(\cot^{-1}(-\sqrt{3}) = \frac{5\pi}{6}\) hai, \(-\frac{\pi}{6}\) nahin.
2. \(\cot^{-1} x = \tan^{-1}\frac{1}{x}\) negative \(x\) par lagana: yeh sirf \(x > 0\) ke liye sahi hai.
3. Andar wala angle principal range se bahar chun lena, jaise \(\tan^{-1}(-\sqrt{3}) = \frac{2\pi}{3}\).
4. Domain ke sawal mein andar wale function ka domain bhool jana (jaise \(\ln x\) ke liye \(x > 0\)).
5. Point \((x, y)\) se \(\sin\alpha\) aur \(\cos\alpha\) ulat dena: \(\sin\alpha = \frac{y}{r}\), \(\cos\alpha = \frac{x}{r}\).
